indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the following word are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver slips the gearstick into neutral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing into neutral' reads as a gear change, but 'changing' is the anagram signal working on NEUTRAL, and 'into' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Renault is a French make of motor vehicle, so it is an example of a car.

parts.note: a commercial traveller is a sales rep

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word does might be arranged some other way, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A tourist lies back and rests, as travellers are wont to do.
explanation.walkthrough: A commercial traveller, an old term for a salesman, is a rep; 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange 'does', and 'as' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To repose is to lie at rest, so reposed is a past-tense synonym of rested.

parts.note: read 'soapy' as belonging to a TV soap opera: the long-running Australian soap is titled after the people next door, and its kind of friendship is the quality of being friendly to those next door

explanation.surface: A sentimental, sudsy kind of companionship.
explanation.walkthrough: NEIGHBOURS is a long-running Australian TV soap opera, popular in Britain; the answer is the quality its title suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendliness towards those living next door is a kind of friendship, and the soap's title names those people.

clue.text: Craft in which some denizens of Uranus may turn up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turn up means the letters are read from the bottom upward, that is backwards
some tells us only part of the run of letters in the following words is used

explanation.surface: Spacecraft carrying aliens from the planet Uranus might arrive one day.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'denizens of Uranus' backwards gives SUNARUFOSNEZINED, and 'some' of it, the middle stretch, is the answer; 'turn up' signals the reversal in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Unidentified flying objects are supposed alien spacecraft, so they are craft.

clue.text: Time to find Russian currency in difficulties

definitions.note: plural in the clue, while the answer is a mass noun covering any amount of hardship

parts.note: the rouble is the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: A traveller struggling to get hold of Russian money while in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble is problems or hardship, a general word for difficulties.

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A distressed nun and a dame, both unnamed, are upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anonymous has no name given, so it is nameless.

clue.text: Man to be conveyed by shipping line losing head, not picked up

indicators.note: conveyed by means carried inside, so one piece goes within the other
losing head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Cunard is a famous British shipping line
a man is referred to as he

explanation.surface: A passenger on a liner's voyage goes overboard and is not rescued.
explanation.walkthrough: Cunard ran the great transatlantic liners; 'losing head' drops its first letter and 'to be conveyed by' means the man rides inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unheard was never caught by the ear, so it was not picked up by a listener.

definitions.meaning: cheek or nerve, as in having the nerve to do something
to kiss and cuddle, British slang for a passionate kiss

explanation.surface: Someone bold enough to steal a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazen nerve is a slang sense of the word, and kissing amorously is its verb sense, like snogging.

clue.text: Ratio of chemical composition we found in odd logarithm clue

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters given are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemistry student finds a ratio buried in a strange maths puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges WE plus LOGARITHM CLUE, fifteen letters in all; 'found in' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The relative mass of a molecule, compared with a standard atomic unit, is a ratio fixed by the substance's makeup.

clue.text: Humorous quality evinced by unknown name in clothing

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the clothing word

parts.note: dress means clothing
y is a classic algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone's dry wit shows in the outfit of an anonymous person.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry humour is wit delivered deadpan, so the quality of that wit is humorous.

clue.text: Playschool Phil and I run according to traditional wisdom?

indicators.note: run, as a stocking runs or dye runs, signals that the letters come apart and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two children, Phil and the speaker, dash about at playschool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' rearranges PLAYSCHOOL PHIL plus I, fifteen letters; 'and' is no fodder. The question mark admits the definition is loose: philosophy is traditional wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in keeping with the love of wisdom, or with calm stoic acceptance, follows established learning.

parts.note: soh is the fifth note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: A remark about a historic part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: SOH is the fifth note of tonic sol-fa (do, re, mi, fa, soh). SOHO is a central London district famous for nightlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is an area of central London's West End, a historic district of the city.

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of US president Abraham Lincoln
am is short for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: Abraham Lincoln goes jogging before dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, a direction at right angles to the keel lies across it, so a line in that direction runs across.

indicators.note: concealing means hiding one thing within another

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A skin specialist keeps a patient's name secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimples on the skin are spots, and the condition causing them is this skin complaint.

indicators.note: seen around means the composer is placed surrounding the other piece

parts.note: J. S. Bach is a famous composer

explanation.surface: A composer spotted walking on an English shore.
explanation.definitionFit: The foreshore is the strip of sandy or shingly coast between the tide marks.

clue.text: Young going around old city in warm coats?

indicators.note: going around means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: fry are young fish
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, the crossword's favourite old city

explanation.surface: Young folk dressed in warm jackets touring an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature in thick warm coats of hair is covered in fur, hence hairy and soft.

clue.text: Doe is frolicking around church — that's the bishop's jurisdiction

indicators.note: around means the anagram is placed surrounding the next piece
frolicking means leaping about playfully, so the letters jump into a new order

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A deer skips around a churchyard on church land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolicking' rearranges DOE IS into DIOSE, and 'around' puts CE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop oversees a district of parishes, the area under that bishop's authority.

parts.note: read 'Man' as the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea, not a person, and 'offshore capital' as its seat of government rather than money hidden abroad

explanation.surface: A man's money stashed in a tax haven.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests offshore banking; the Isle of Man is indeed a tax haven, but the answer is its capital town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man's capital town is on the island's east coast, the seat of its government.

clue.text: Uncomfortable result of a cheer reverberating around one?

indicators.note: around means the anagram encloses the next piece
reverberating means echoing and bouncing about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A loud cheer ringing round someone leaves them with a sore ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverberating' rearranges A CHEER into EARCHE, and 'around' wraps it round A, from 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain in the ear is the sort of discomfort a loud cheer next to your head could cause.

clue.text: Charm evident in one arum growing wild

indicators.note: growing wild means running free and unruly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A single arum lily blooming untamed has its own charm.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate or delight someone is to charm them, filling them with love.

clue.text: Impose European leader on Northern Constabulary

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word

parts.note: a police constabulary is a force

explanation.surface: A European chief takes charge of a northern police force.
explanation.definitionFit: To force obedience to a rule is to impose it.

clue.text: Where Josiah produced pottery, having left off portraiture, maybe?

indicators.note: maybe suggests the remaining letters could be ordered another way
off means taken away, so a stretch of the word is removed

parts.note: port is the nautical word for left

explanation.surface: A painter gives up portraits to make pots instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' takes PORT from PORTRAITURE, leaving RAITURE, which 'maybe' rearranges. Josiah Wedgwood, the English potter, named his Staffordshire works and village Etruria.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedgwood's factory village near Stoke-on-Trent bore this name, after the ancient region of Italy famed for its pots.

clue.text: Term describing article in English mine

indicators.note: in places the article inside the other pieces

parts.note: a pit is a mine
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper term describing a feature on an English mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts THE inside EPIT, between the I and the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive word or phrase applied to someone is a term for them, such as a nickname or byname.

indicators.note: incorporating means taking another piece inside
frightfully means in a disordered, alarming way, so the letters of the word are rearranged
primarily means first, so only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A cast of shining stars, all luminaries, is awfully celestial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightfully' rearranges ASTRAL, and 'incorporating' takes in L, the first letter of 'luminaries' ('primarily'). The whole clue also describes a team of star names.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast made up entirely of famous performers is all big names, a line-up of luminaries.

clue.text: Feature of opera — a tune with backing

indicators.note: with backing means the word is turned to run backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: An opera singer's melody accompanied by an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Operas are built around solo songs, so such a song is a standard feature of one.

parts.note: to rig, as in a match or election, is to fix it

explanation.surface: Attaching a partner to an oil rig.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten or stick one thing to another is to attach it.

indicators.note: bagging means holding inside, so the answer sits within these words

explanation.surface: A cricketer's teammate always seems to be out for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nought, which the surface plays on; here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A teal is a small freshwater dabbling bird of the duck family.

indicators.note: in means the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A sports field in a valley in rural Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; in Australia a cricket field is generally called an oval.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-shaped sports field, especially for cricket, is called by its shape.

indicators.note: not means the following piece is left out

parts.note: a pearl is a jewel

explanation.surface: A gem that is wrong for a wedding ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A peal is a ringing of bells, so ring is a synonym.

definitions.meaning: having had a drink too many
the cox of a rowing boat is the one extra person beyond its eight rowers

explanation.surface: A coxswain who is tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for slightly drunk also describes the cox, who sits as the ninth member of a rowing eight.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mildly intoxicated, from one drink too many; a coxed boat holds an eight plus its steerer.

definitions.meaning: to work out a puzzle a second time, the prefix re meaning again

explanation.surface: Determined to tackle the crossword a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Making up one's mind is to determine; solving afresh is re plus solve.

indicators.note: around signals the letters of the word are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: An early satellite shakes and rattles as it orbits.
explanation.walkthrough: TELSTAR, launched in 1962, relayed the first live transatlantic television pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1962 Telstar spacecraft was among the first to relay television and telephone signals.
